answer: Cross-cluster quorum admission requires entrants to gather signatures from four validator branches sharing zero counterparty volume, each branch locking 100 pearl in a slashable timber escrow to issue its crystal signature. Since the timber contract tracks shared backing sets, when the same four branches sign for an $n$-th entrant, each must lock $100n^2$ pearl for that $n$-th crystal. An independent agent needs 400 locked pearl across four branches, while a sybil operator spawning $k$ clones via one colluding quartet must lock $\frac{200}{3}k(k+1)(2k+1)$ pearl or bribe $4k$ disjoint branches.
